title: The Songbook of Rosewater Lane
premise: Paloma Dravenmoor inherited Rosewater Vineyard along with its crushing debts, and she's spent three years quietly selling off her grandmother's songbooks and cellar stock to keep the estate alive. When a snowstorm traps her with Theo Marchetti—the rival winemaker who broke her heart a decade ago—and his business partner, old wounds and unfinished songs resurface. As the storm forces honesty, Paloma must choose between selling the vineyard to a developer who will save her financially and fighting for a heritage festival that could save it spiritually, with Theo's help. She chooses both love and legacy, discovering that her grandmother's final songbook holds the deed solution that lets her keep Rosewater Lane without losing Theo again.
about_author: Paloma Vasquez is a former sommelier who left restaurant life to write love stories set in wine country, drawing on years of harvest seasons spent in cellars across three continents. She lives in a converted farmhouse where she keeps her late mother's recipe box on the kitchen windowsill.

chapters.title: Debts Instead of Grapes
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Three years after inheriting Rosewater Vineyard, Paloma catalogs what's left: failing vines, mounting loans, and her grandmother's songbooks, which she's been secretly selling one by one. A letter arrives from developer Marcus Hale offering a lifeline price for the property. Emotional beat: weary resignation masking grief.

chapters.title: The Tasting That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She hosts a critical tasting meant to impress investors, only to discover Theo Marchetti—her college love turned rival winemaker—is representing the biggest one. A decade ago he chose a Napa career over her. They spar professionally while old hurt simmers. Emotional beat: guarded hostility crackling with unresolved attraction.

chapters.title: Snowbound at Rosewater
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. An early blizzard strands Theo, his partner Dana, and Paloma at the vineyard farmhouse with no road out and a broken furnace. Forced into close quarters, they share wine from the last good vintage and memories slip out despite themselves. Emotional beat: reluctant warmth thawing frozen defenses.

chapters.title: Songs in the Attic
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Searching for blankets, they find her grandmother's attic and an unopened songbook dated the year Paloma was born. Reading lyrics aloud by candlelight, Theo sees the girl he loved, and Paloma admits how much she's sold. Emotional beat: vulnerable confession met with tenderness instead of judgment.

chapters.title: What Dana Knows
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. Watching Theo and Paloma orbit each other, Dana reveals why she really came: Hale's development deal is contingent on Theo's endorsement, and Theo has been hiding his own financial ruin. Dana warns Paloma not to trust him—or herself. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance and dawning betrayal.

chapters.title: The Mistake of Our Twenties
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Power out, tempers flare; Paloma confronts Theo about leaving, and he finally explains the family pressure and fear that drove him away. The argument collapses into a kiss neither can take back. Emotional beat: cathartic collision of anger and longing.

chapters.title: Morning After the Thaw
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The roads clear and reality returns. Hale calls demanding an answer; Dana pushes Theo to sign. Paloma overhears Theo say the vineyard 'isn't salvageable' and retreats, deciding to accept Hale's offer before she can be abandoned twice. Emotional beat: heartbreak disguised as pragmatism.

chapters.title: Hale's Signature
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. At the signing, Hale reveals the fine print: the songbooks are included in the sale as 'ephemera.' Realizing she'd be erasing her grandmother entirely, Paloma walks out mid-signature. Theo arrives, having refused Hale, and publicly stakes his reputation on Rosewater's festival plan. Emotional beat: defiant reclaiming of self.

chapters.title: The Last Songbook
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Racing the festival deadline, Paloma and Theo decode the final songbook's marginalia: her grandmother's will provision granting a conservation easement if the family 'keeps singing'—a heritage designation that blocks development and forgives penalties. They submit it hours before deadline. Emotional beat: desperate hope rewarded through inherited wisdom.

chapters.title: Rosewater Lane, In Bloom
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Spring: the first Heritage Festival fills the lane with music, Dana joins as partner, and the vines show new life. Theo asks for a second chance not as penance but as choice, and Paloma says yes. She hangs the last unsold songbook above the tasting room door. Emotional beat: joyful arrival—love and legacy kept together.
